457	fn main() {
458	    // Shell completion: when the shell set COMPLETE, answer with
459	    // the candidates and exit before anything else runs.
460	    CompleteEnv::with_factory(Cli::command).complete();
461	    let cli = Cli::parse();
462	
463	    // The bench-name listing is a pure print-and-exit path: no
464	    // logging, no config, no setup.
465	    if cli.list_benches {
466	        for name in benches::names() {
467	            println!("{name}");
468	        }
469	        return;
470	    }
471	
472	    // 'describe-record' is a pure print-and-exit command word: the
473	    // record's field dictionary, documenting outputs the way
474	    // --help documents inputs.
475	    if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "describe-record") {
476	        if cli.benches.len() > 1 {
477	            eprintln!("error: 'describe-record' runs alone; drop the other bench args");
478	            std::process::exit(2);
479	        }
480	        println!("{ABOUT}\n");
481	        record::describe();
482	        return;
483	    }
484	
485	    // 'read-freq' prints and exits: no root, no config, no banner,
486	    // so a prompt or status bar can call it every few seconds.
487	    if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "read-freq") {
488	        if cli.benches.len() > 1 {
489	            eprintln!("error: 'read-freq' runs alone; drop the other bench args");
490	            std::process::exit(2);
491	        }
492	        std::process::exit(freqctl::cmd_read_freq(cli.as_config));
493	    }
494	
495	    // 'pin-freq' and 'restore-freq' mutate the box on request and
496	    // exit. Both read the config for the declared [freq] steady
497	    // state; pin-freq additionally takes one optional MHZ arg
498	    // (`pin-freq 3800`).
499	    if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "pin-freq") {
500	        if cli.benches[0] != "pin-freq" || cli.benches.len() > 2 {
501	            eprintln!("error: 'pin-freq' runs alone, with at most one MHZ arg");
502	            std::process::exit(2);
503	        }
504	        let mhz = match cli.benches.get(1) {
505	            None => None,
506	            Some(s) => match s.parse::<u64>() {
507	                Ok(v) => Some(v),
508	                Err(_) => {
509	                    eprintln!("error: pin-freq: {s:?} is not a frequency in MHz");
510	                    std::process::exit(2);
511	                }
512	            },
513	        };
514	        let config = load_config_or_exit();
515	        std::process::exit(freqctl::cmd_pin_freq(config.freq.as_ref(), mhz));
516	    }
517	    if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "restore-freq") {
518	        if cli.benches.len() > 1 {
519	            eprintln!("error: 'restore-freq' runs alone; drop the other bench args");
520	            std::process::exit(2);
521	        }
522	        let config = load_config_or_exit();
523	        std::process::exit(freqctl::cmd_restore_freq(config.freq.as_ref()));
524	    }
525	
526	    // Default filter is `warn`; `-v` bumps to `debug`. `RUST_LOG`
527	    // (if set) always wins — so users can still do fine-grained
528	    // per-module filtering without fighting the flag.
529	    let mut builder = env_logger::Builder::from_default_env();
530	    if std::env::var_os("RUST_LOG").is_none() {
531	        builder.filter_level(if cli.verbose {
532	            log::LevelFilter::Debug
533	        } else {
534	            log::LevelFilter::Warn
535	        });
536	    }
537	    builder.format_timestamp(None).init();
538	
539	    if cli.benches.is_empty() {
540	        println!("{ABOUT}\n");
541	        println!("no benches specified. use -h or --help for more info.\n");
542	        println!("Benches:");
543	        println!("{}", wrap_names(&benches::names(), 72));
544	        return;
545	    }
546	
547	    // 'qualify-environment' is a command, not a bench: it respawns
548	    // --runs times and grades the box across those runs. It stands
549	    // alone, and it re-execs children itself, so it runs before
550	    // the inhibit/config/banner path a bench run needs.
551	    if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "qualify-environment") {
552	        if cli.benches.len() > 1 {
553	            eprintln!("error: 'qualify-environment' runs alone; drop the other bench args");
554	            std::process::exit(2);
555	        }
556	        println!("{ABOUT}\n");
557	        let code = qualify::run(&qualify::QualifyCfg {
558	            runs: cli.runs,
559	            gap_s: cli.gap,
560	            duration_s: cli.duration.unwrap_or(QUALIFY_CHILD_SECONDS),
561	            pin_cpus: cli.pin_cpus.clone(),
562	            print_only: cli.print_only,
563	            settle_time: cli.settle_time,
564	        });
565	        std::process::exit(code);
566	    }
567	
568	    // Re-exec under systemd-inhibit (unless --no-inhibit or
569	    // already inhibited) before any output, so the banner prints
570	    // once, from the inhibited child.
571	    let inhibit_status = inhibit::ensure(cli.no_inhibit);
572	
573	    // Layered defaults (built-in < XDG file < project-local file <
574	    // CLI). A malformed config is fatal so a typo surfaces.
575	    let (config, config_files) = match config::load() {
576	        Ok(c) => c,
577	        Err(e) => {
578	            eprintln!("error: config: {e}");
579	            std::process::exit(2);
580	        }
581	    };
582	
583	    // Pin the clock before anything measures or prints, so the
584	    // Setup block and the warm loop both see the pinned state. The
585	    // guard restores the declared steady state on drop (normal
586	    // exit and panic) and via the signal path on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
587	    let freq_pin = match cli.pin_freq {
588	        None => None,
589	        Some(mhz) => match freqctl::RunPin::engage(config.freq.as_ref(), mhz) {
590	            Ok(g) => Some(g),
591	            Err(e) => {
592	                eprintln!("error: --pin-freq: {e}");
593	                std::process::exit(2);
594	            }
595	        },
596	    };
597	
598	    println!("{ABOUT}\n");
599	
600	    if let Some(mask) = pin::current_affinity() {
601	        info!("startup affinity: {}", pin::affinity_summary(&mask));
602	    }
603	
604	    let pin_cpus: Vec<usize> = match cli.pin_cpus.as_deref() {
605	        None => Vec::new(),
606	        // A spec naming a config profile expands to its CPU list;
607	        // anything else parses as a raw CPU spec.
608	        Some(spec) => match pin::parse_cpus(config.resolve_pin(spec)) {
609	            Ok(v) => v,
610	            Err(e) => {
611	                eprintln!("error: --pin-cpus: {e}");
612	                std::process::exit(2);
613	            }
614	        },
615	    };
616	
617	    // Pin main to the pool's first slot when --pin-cpus is given: thread 0 of a bench measures
618	    // on main, and the warm loop is a real timing phase converging on per-CPU frequency state,
619	    // so it must run where measurement will run. Without --pin-cpus, main stays wherever the
620	    // scheduler has it: a busy thread stays put, and the warm state lands on the CPU that
621	    // measures. The retired CPU0-default warm pin parked the warm on the kernel's busiest CPU
622	    // for no measured benefit: the tick-rate read is a ratio that cancels interruptions (~8e-7
623	    // spread across CPUs), and nothing else ran pinned.
624	    if let Some(&cpu) = pin_cpus.first() {
625	        pin::pin_current(Some(cpu));
626	        info!("pinned main to CPU {cpu} (bench pin pool slot 0)");
627	    }
628	    if let Some(mask) = pin::current_affinity() {
629	        debug!("affinity for warm + run: {}", pin::affinity_summary(&mask));
630	    }
631	
632	    // Warm the one-time TSC tick-rate calibration (a ~10 ms spin behind a OnceLock) here on
633	    // main. Without this the first TProbe::new in a bench thread pays it inside the measurement
634	    // window: a short -d (e.g. 0.01) was consumed entirely by that spin and recorded zero
635	    // samples.
636	    let ticks_per_ns = ticks::ticks_per_ns();
637	    debug!("ticks_per_ns: {ticks_per_ns:.6}");
638	
639	    // Same precedence as duration: CLI, then config, then the
640	    // built-in. Negative is rejected rather than clamped: it
641	    // means the caller expected something we don't do.
642	    let settle_time = cli
643	        .settle_time
644	        .or(config.settle_time)
645	        .unwrap_or(harness::DEFAULT_SETTLE_TIME_S);
646	    if settle_time < 0.0 {
647	        eprintln!("error: --settle-time must be zero or more, got {settle_time}");
648	        std::process::exit(2);
649	    }
650	
651	    // Same precedence as settle time: CLI, then config, then the built-in.
652	    let warm_cap = cli
653	        .warm_cap
654	        .or(config.warm_cap)
655	        .unwrap_or(harness::DEFAULT_WARM_CAP_S);
656	    if warm_cap < 0.0 {
657	        eprintln!("error: --warm-cap must be zero or more, got {warm_cap}");
658	        std::process::exit(2);
659	    }
660	
661	    // Blocks: CLI wins, then config, then the built-in. Every run
662	    // has them, so the sleep and warmup knobs below need no gate.
663	    let blocks = cli
664	        .blocks
665	        .or(config.blocks)
666	        .unwrap_or(harness::DEFAULT_BLOCKS);
667	
668	    // Block knobs: CLI wins, then config, then the built-in
669	    // default. The sleep defaults to a short range so every run's
670	    // blocks are replicates, and the warmup to zero so no sample
671	    // is discarded unless asked.
672	    let block_sleep_s = match cli.block_sleep.as_deref() {
673	        Some(s) => match timespec::parse_span(s) {
674	            Ok(v) => v,
675	            Err(e) => {
676	                eprintln!("error: --block-sleep: {e}");
677	                std::process::exit(2);
678	            }
679	        },
680	        None => config.block_sleep.unwrap_or(harness::DEFAULT_BLOCK_SLEEP_S),
681	    };
682	    let block_warmup_s = match cli.block_warmup.as_deref() {
683	        Some(s) => match timespec::parse_scalar(s) {
684	            Ok(v) => v,
685	            Err(e) => {
686	                eprintln!("error: --block-warmup: {e}");
687	                std::process::exit(2);
688	            }
689	        },
690	        None => config.block_warmup.unwrap_or(0.0),
691	    };
692	
693	    // Main's placement covers the warm loop and thread 0 of every bench, so the cell names
694	    // both.
695	    let main_pin_display = match pin_cpus.first() {
696	        Some(c) => format!("CPU {c} (pool slot 0; warm + run)"),
697	        None => "none (scheduler placement)".to_string(),
698	    };
699	    // The box's clock and power policy, printed before any bench so every archived report says
700	    // what machine produced it. No report before 0.25.0 recorded the policy, which left an 8.9%
701	    // governor delta indistinguishable from a code change in any A/B spanning one.
702	    let policy = freq::policy();
703	    let boost = policy.boost.as_ref().map(|f| freq::PolicyField {
704	        value: boost_word(&f.value).to_string(),
705	        uniform: f.uniform,
706	    });
707	    println!("Setup:");
708	    println!("  ticks/ns          {ticks_per_ns:.6}");
709	    println!("  tick period       {:.3} ns", 1.0 / ticks_per_ns);
710	    println!(
711	        "  cpufreq driver    {}",
712	        policy_cell(policy.driver.as_ref())
713	    );
714	    println!(
715	        "  governor          {}",
716	        policy_cell(policy.governor.as_ref())
717	    );
718	    println!("  EPP               {}", policy_cell(policy.epp.as_ref()));
719	    println!("  boost             {}", policy_cell(boost.as_ref()));
720	    println!("  main pin          {main_pin_display}");
721	    println!("  bench pin         {}", pin::plan_summary(&pin_cpus));
722	    if let Some(g) = &freq_pin {
723	        println!(
724	            "  freq pin          {} MHz ({}; min = max, boost off; restores on exit)",
725	            g.khz / 1000,
726	            g.source
727	        );
728	    }
729	    // The block knobs print on every run, zeros included: an
730	    // invisible sleep shaping results is the failure mode the
731	    // knobs replaced.
732	    println!("  blocks            {blocks} per run");
733	    println!("  block sleep       {}", sleep_cell(block_sleep_s));
734	    println!("  block warmup      {}", warmup_cell(block_warmup_s));
735	    // The budgets, not the spend: each run's report brackets carry
736	    // its own warm=used/cap, and the grade block's settle cell says
737	    // when the box settled.
738	    println!("  warm budget       settle {settle_time}s once + cap {warm_cap}s per run");
739	    println!("  sleep inhibit     {inhibit_status}");
740	    println!("  config            {}", config_summary(&config_files));
741	    println!();
742	
743	    // The record sink resolves before any bench runs, so a bad
744	    // path or tag fails in milliseconds rather than after minutes
745	    // of measuring.
746	    let recorder = match cli.record.as_deref() {
747	        None => None,
748	        Some(path) => match record::Recorder::new(path, &cli.tag) {
749	            Ok(r) => Some(r),
750	            Err(e) => {
751	                eprintln!("error: --record: {e}");
752	                std::process::exit(2);
753	            }
754	        },
755	    };
756	
757	    // 'suggest-freq BENCH' replaces the bench loop with the
758	    // candidate descent, driving that one bench through the same
759	    // run configuration. Resolved here rather than with the other
760	    // command words because it wants the whole setup a bench run
761	    // gets: inhibit, config, Setup block, knobs.
762	    let suggest = match cli.benches.first() {
763	        Some(w) if w == "suggest-freq" => {
764	            if cli.benches.len() != 2 {
765	                eprintln!(
766	                    "error: 'suggest-freq' takes exactly one bench word, e.g. \
767	                     'suggest-freq zcr-mpsc-v0-2t'"
768	                );
769	                std::process::exit(2);
770	            }
771	            if cli.pin_freq.is_some() {
772	                eprintln!("error: suggest-freq pins for itself; drop --pin-freq");
773	                std::process::exit(2);
774	            }
775	            Some(cli.benches[1].clone())
776	        }
777	        _ => {
778	            if cli.benches.iter().any(|b| b == "suggest-freq") {
779	                eprintln!("error: 'suggest-freq' leads: 'suggest-freq BENCH'");
780	                std::process::exit(2);
781	            }
782	            None
783	        }
784	    };
785	
786	    let resolve_args: Vec<String> = match &suggest {
787	        Some(name) => vec![name.clone()],
788	        None => cli.benches.clone(),
789	    };
790	    let runners = match benches::resolve(&resolve_args) {
791	        Ok(r) => r,
792	        Err(e) => {
793	            eprintln!("error: {e}");
794	            std::process::exit(2);
795	        }
796	    };
797	    if suggest.is_some() && runners.len() != 1 {
798	        eprintln!(
799	            "error: suggest-freq names one bench exactly (a prefix matching several \
800	             does not say which schedule the suggestion serves)"
801	        );
802	        std::process::exit(2);
803	    }
804	
805	    // Duration precedence: CLI -d / -D win, then the config
806	    // `duration`, then the built-in default.
807	    let target_seconds = match (cli.duration, cli.total_duration) {
808	        (Some(d), _) => d,
809	        (None, Some(t)) => t / runners.len() as f64,
810	        (None, None) => config.duration.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_DURATION),
811	    };
812	
813	    let cfg = harness::RunCfg {
814	        target_seconds,
815	        samples_override: cli.samples,
816	        inner_override: cli.inner,
817	        pin_cpus: &pin_cpus,
818	        report_ticks: cli.ticks,
819	        seam_probes: !cli.no_env_probe,
820	        band_labels: cli
821	            .band_labels
822	            .or(config.band_labels)
823	            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_BAND_LABELS),
824	        decimals: cli.decimals.or(config.decimals).unwrap_or(DEFAULT_DECIMALS) as usize,
825	        settle_time_s: settle_time,
826	        warm_cap_s: warm_cap,
827	        blocks,
828	        block_sleep_s,
829	        block_warmup_s,
830	        record: recorder.as_ref(),
831	    };
832	
833	    if let Some(name) = &suggest {
834	        std::process::exit(freqctl::cmd_suggest_freq(
835	            config.freq.as_ref(),
836	            name,
837	            runners[0],
838	            &cfg,
839	        ));
840	    }
841	
842	    for run in runners {
843	        run(&cfg);
844	    }
845	}
846	
847	/// Render one `Setup:` policy cell: the token, marked when CPUs disagree, or why it is absent.
848	///
849	/// - `None` prints `not exposed` and never a default. A box without the file has no such
850	///   policy, and inventing one is exactly what makes an archived number ambiguous.
851	/// - A non-uniform field carries `(mixed across CPUs)`: one CPU's token is not the box's policy
852	///   when the policy groups were set separately.
853	fn policy_cell(field: Option<&freq::PolicyField>) -> String {
854	    match field {
855	        None => "not exposed".to_string(),
856	        Some(f) if f.uniform => f.value.clone(),
857	        Some(f) => format!("{} (mixed across CPUs)", f.value),
858	    }
859	}
860	
861	/// Render the Setup `block sleep` cell from the resolved span (seconds).
862	fn sleep_cell(span: (f64, f64)) -> String {
863	    if span.1 <= 0.0 {
864	        "none (blocks are partitions; CI95/LSC print '-')".to_string()
865	    } else if span.0 == span.1 {
866	        format!("{} fixed", timespec::display(span.0))
867	    } else {
868	        format!(
869	            "{}-{} random per block",
870	            timespec::display(span.0),
871	            timespec::display(span.1)
872	        )
873	    }
874	}
875	
876	/// Render the Setup `block warmup` cell from the resolved seconds.
877	fn warmup_cell(s: f64) -> String {
878	    if s <= 0.0 {
879	        "none (records from the first post-wake call)".to_string()
880	    } else {
881	        format!("{} unrecorded post-wake", timespec::display(s))
882	    }
883	}
884	
885	/// `boost`'s raw sysfs token as a word; anything unrecognized passes through untranslated
886	/// rather than being guessed at.
887	fn boost_word(raw: &str) -> &str {
888	    match raw {
889	        "1" => "enabled",
890	        "0" => "disabled",
891	        other => other,
892	    }
893	}
894	
895	#[cfg(test)]
896	mod tests {
897	    use super::*;
898	
899	    fn policy_field(value: &str, uniform: bool) -> freq::PolicyField {
900	        freq::PolicyField {
901	            value: value.to_string(),
902	            uniform,
903	        }
904	    }
905	
906	    #[test]
907	    fn policy_cell_says_absent_rather_than_defaulting() {
908	        assert_eq!(policy_cell(None), "not exposed");
909	    }
910	
911	    #[test]
912	    fn policy_cell_marks_a_split_policy() {
913	        assert_eq!(
914	            policy_cell(Some(&policy_field("powersave", true))),
915	            "powersave"
916	        );
917	        assert_eq!(
918	            policy_cell(Some(&policy_field("powersave", false))),
919	            "powersave (mixed across CPUs)"
920	        );
921	    }
922	
923	    #[test]
924	    fn boost_word_translates_only_the_known_tokens() {
925	        assert_eq!(boost_word("1"), "enabled");
926	        assert_eq!(boost_word("0"), "disabled");
927	        assert_eq!(boost_word("unexpected"), "unexpected");
928	    }
929	
930	    #[test]
931	    fn wrap_names_single_line() {
932	        assert_eq!(wrap_names(&["a", "b"], 72), "  a, b");
933	    }

937	        let values = |typed: &str| -> Vec<String> {
938	            complete_positional(std::ffi::OsStr::new(typed))
939	                .iter()
940	                .map(|c| c.get_value().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
941	                .collect()
942	        };
943	        assert_eq!(values("cb-chan"), ["cb-chan-1t", "cb-chan-2t"]);
944	        assert_eq!(values("qual"), ["qualify-environment"]);

947	        assert!(all.contains(&"suggest-freq".to_string()));
948	    }

## The Setup banner

Every run opens with a `Setup:` block: the TSC tick rate, the
box's power policy (cpufreq driver, governor, EPP, boost), the
pinning plan (`main pin` / `bench pin`), the frequency pin when
`--pin-freq` is live, the block knobs whenever blocks run
(`block sleep` / `block warmup`, zeros included, each naming its
consequence), the warm budget, the sleep-inhibit state, and
which config files were loaded. It is provenance for the numbers
below it, not measurement: no report before the policy lines
existed could distinguish an 8.9% governor delta from a code
change, which is why they print on every run.

The apparatus cost that used to be measured and subtracted here
is now handled by construction instead. A micro-probe times
back-to-back timer pairs at startup and sizes the inner loop so
framing is a small fraction of the workload's per-call cost. The
cost is never named as a number and never removed from a sample.
See
[in-interval vs call-to-call](../notes/design.md#timer-overhead-in-interval-vs-call-to-call)
for why the in-interval slice and the call-to-call cost are
different quantities, and why only the latter is worth measuring
for sizing.

A sub-quantum phase dither still runs between bench samples at
the seam, so a run's aggregate means do not inherit a coherent
bias from where samples happen to land on the clock lattice
([dithering](../notes/design.md#dithering-random-phase-injection)).
Per-call costs are machine- and frequency-regime-specific: see
[Frequency dependence](../notes/design.md#frequency-dependence-what-is-constant-what-is-not).
To decide whether a difference between two implementations is
real (and how many runs that takes), see
[Comparing implementations: LSC](../notes/design.md#comparing-implementations-least-significant-change).

Steadiness is graded per run rather than at startup, from the
run's own data, and prints at the foot of each report. See
[The run grade's signals](#the-run-grades-signals).

The `Setup:` banner reports the `main pin` (main's placement,
covering the warm loop and thread 0 of every bench) and
`bench pin` (per-bench thread pool) separately, plus the
`warm budget` (the once-per-process settle time and the per-run
cap). Each run's report bracket then carries its own
`warm=used/budget` spend, where the first run's budget includes
the settle time and later runs' is the cap alone.

is one band, labeled by its **upper boundary**, the lower boundary

# Config file

Defaults, named pin profiles, and the box's declared frequency
steady state can live in a config file, so common invocations
don't repeat flags and the frequency commands have a way home.
Moved from the README (whose [Usage](../README.md#usage) points
here) and refreshed for the markdown carrier, the block knobs,
and the `[freq]` table.

## Carriers and precedence

Two carriers, one per directory. A `.md` config is a markdown
document whose ` ```toml ` fences, concatenated in document
order, are the config, so the prose between them documents the
file to its reader. `.md` is the recommended form. Plain `.toml`
stays accepted. A directory holding both is a hard error naming
both paths, because the one you edit could otherwise be the one
the loader ignores.

Precedence, lowest to highest:

- **built-in defaults**: `duration=5.0`, `band_labels=both`,
  `decimals=1`, `settle_time=1.5`, `warm_cap=1.5`,
  `block_sleep=1-10ms`, `block_warmup=0`, and `blocks=100`,
  which makes a five-second run's blocks about 50 ms, each a
  replicate.
- **XDG file**: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/iiac-perf/config.md` (or
  `.toml`), falling back to `$HOME/.config/iiac-perf/` when
  `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset. The per-user home for defaults,
  profiles, and the box's `[freq]` steady state.
- **project-local file**: `iiac-perf.md` (or `iiac-perf.toml`)
  in the current directory (no upward walk). It overrides the XDG
  file field by field, profiles merging by key and the `[freq]`
  table replacing whole (half of one box's declaration on top of
  half of another's would be a state nobody declared).
- **CLI flags**: always win.

The startup banner's `config` line names the files that were
loaded (or `none (built-in defaults)`). A present-but-malformed
file is a hard error rather than a silent fallback, so a typo
surfaces. Every key is optional, and
[`iiac-perf.toml.example`](../iiac-perf.toml.example) is a
ready-to-copy sample.

## Keys

```toml
duration     = 10.0     # default -d seconds
band_labels  = "zpn"    # zpn | frac | both
decimals     = 2        # 0-3
settle_time  = 3.0      # default --settle-time seconds; 0 skips the warm
warm_cap     = 1.5      # default --warm-cap seconds; 0 caps immediately
blocks       = 10       # default --blocks count, 1-1000; 100 when absent
block_sleep  = "1-10ms" # default --block-sleep span; 0 = partitions
block_warmup = "2ms"    # default --block-warmup; 0 records post-wake calls

[profiles]              # named --pin-cpus CPU specs
smt = "0,12"           # SMT siblings of one physical core (contention)
ccx = "0,1"            # independent cores, same CCX (best channel latency)
ccd = "0,6"            # cross-CCD
```

## The [freq] steady state

The `[freq]` table declares the box's steady state: what
`restore-freq` converges to, from any starting point, and what a
pinned run (`--pin-freq`, `pin-freq`, `suggest-freq`) restores on
exit. Declared once by you rather than remembered from before a
pin, because a remembered state ratchets on back-to-back runs.
It normally lives in the XDG config, the steady state being the
box's rather than the project's.

`iiac-perf read-freq --as-config` prints the current state in
this form, ready to paste into a `toml` fence:

```toml
[freq]
governor = "powersave"
epp      = "balance_performance"  # required exactly when the box has EPP
boost    = true                   # required exactly when the box has a boost knob
# min_mhz / max_mhz omitted: the hardware range
pin_mhz  = 3801                   # pin target; omitted = the discovered base clock
```

A knob the box exposes must be declared (restoring around it
would leave a pin's residue), and a knob the box lacks must not
be. `suggest-freq` measures the best `pin_mhz` for a workload
and ends with the line to paste.

please review

Google isn't wrong, it's just showing the most common way to write it. `fold`'s second argument is anything callable with the accumulator and the next item that returns the new accumulator. In the signature that's `F: FnMut(B, Self::Item) -> B`. A closure is one such callable, and a named function whose signature fits is another.

`usize::max` is that kind of function. It's `Ord::max` for `usize`, with the type `fn(usize, usize) -> usize`. Our accumulator `B` is `usize` (from the `0`) and each item is a `usize` (from `p.value.len()`), so it fits. These three lines are the same:

```rust
.fold(0, usize::max)
.fold(0, |acc, len| acc.max(len))
.fold(0, |acc, len| usize::max(acc, len))
```

Clippy often suggests the first form itself, through its `redundant_closure` lint, when a closure only forwards its arguments to a function.

If the closure reads more clearly to you, I can switch to `.fold(0, |acc, len| acc.max(len))`. It compiles to the same code.

The plain version: `fold` needs a two-argument function, and `usize::max` is one, so passing it by name is the same as writing the closure that calls it.

content.text:
You're right that `max` doesn't add anything up. In `fold`, though, "accumulator" just means the value carried from one step to the next, whatever it holds. Summing is the textbook example, where the carried value is the total so far. With `max`, the carried value is the largest seen so far.

Here's `fold(0, usize::max)` over value lengths `[3, 4, 7, 4]`:

| step | carried | item | `max(carried, item)` |
|------|---------|------|----------------------|
| start | 0 | | |
| 1 | 0 | 3 | 3 |
| 2 | 3 | 4 | 4 |
| 3 | 4 | 7 | 7 |
| 4 | 7 | 4 | 7 |

The result is 7, the widest value, and an empty list stays at 0 without ever calling `max`. It's the same loop as a sum, keeping the bigger number at each step instead of adding.

If `fold` still reads wrong for a max, the other clear option is a plain loop:

```rust
let mut value_width = 0;
for p in params {
    value_width = value_width.max(p.value.len());
}
```

That's also clippy-clean with no `unwrap`, just more lines.

The plain version: `fold` carries one value through the list. For a sum that value is the total, and here it's the biggest width seen so far.

content.content:
Replicate every run, so a number measured here carries an error bar without a flag being typed.
A hundred blocks keeps a five-second run's time axis at about 50 ms a block, the size the grades
were tuned on, for about 0.7 s more than ten blocks cost. The sleep is a range so each block
re-rolls scheduler and frequency state, and the warmup keeps each post-wake ramp out of the
samples. These keys sit above the `[freq]` fence because the fences concatenate in document order,
and a bare key after a table header would be parsed into that table.
```toml
blocks = 100
block_sleep = "1-10ms"
block_warmup = "2ms"
```
Set the frequency information for these benchmarks
```toml
[freq]
governor = "powersave"
epp = "balance_performance"
boost = true
# min_mhz / max_mhz omitted: the hardware range (563-4673 MHz)
# pin_mhz omitted: the base clock (3801 MHz from acpi_cppc/nominal_freq)
```

The unit tests cover the logic. To see it in real output, run the installed dev build (`iiac-perf-dev`, 0.28.13-1) and look at the `Config:` block. Every command below prints only that block.

**Unit tests** (resolution order, `same as default`, column alignment, value formatting):
```
cargo test run_config
cargo test config_values_read_as_typed
```

**Each source, from this repo's directory** (this directory's `iiac-perf.md` sets `blocks = 100`, `block_sleep = "1-10ms"`, `block_warmup = "2ms"`):
```
# the file: blocks and block_sleep show "(iiac-perf.md, same as default)", block_warmup "(iiac-perf.md)"
iiac-perf-dev min-now -d 0.2 | sed -n '/^Config:/,/^$/p'

# flags win over the file: blocks "(--blocks)", block_warmup "(--block-warmup)", pin_cpus "(--pin-cpus)"
iiac-perf-dev min-now -d 0.2 --blocks 10 --block-warmup 0 --pin-cpus 2,3 | sed -n '/^Config:/,/^$/p'

# a flag equal to the default: decimals "(--decimals, same as default)"
iiac-perf-dev min-now -d 0.2 --decimals 1 | sed -n '/^Config:/,/^$/p'

# -D split across benches: duration "(--total-duration 1 s over 2 benches)"
iiac-perf-dev min-now min-now -D 1 | sed -n '/^Config:/,/^$/p'
```

**No files at all** (every line should say `(default)` and `files` should say `none (built-in defaults)`):
```
cd /tmp && XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/nonexistent iiac-perf-dev min-now -d 0.2 | sed -n '/^Config:/,/^$/p'; cd -
```

**An XDG file plus a profile** (the file path shows with `~` only when it's under your home, and a profile shows its expansion):
```
mkdir -p ~/tmp-xdg/iiac-perf
printf '```toml\nsettle_time = 0.5\n[profiles]\nsmt = "0,12"\n```\n' > ~/tmp-xdg/iiac-perf/config.md
cd /tmp && XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/tmp-xdg iiac-perf-dev min-now -d 0.2 --pin-cpus smt | sed -n '/^Config:/,/^$/p'; cd -
rm -r ~/tmp-xdg
```
You should see `settle_time  500 ms  (~/tmp-xdg/iiac-perf/config.md)` and `pin_cpus  smt = 0,12  (--pin-cpus)`.

**Both files, the nearer one winning:** run that same XDG command from this repo's directory instead of `/tmp`. `settle_time` still comes from the XDG file, and the block keys come from `iiac-perf.md`.

The plain version: `cargo test run_config` checks the logic. The commands above run the real binary with defaults only, with this repo's file, with flags, and with an XDG file, and each line of `Config:` should name the source you just used.
Pushing the rung. The next one is `feat: the record carries the run's config`, and it will reuse this rung's list of settings for the record's `config` object.
